newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB debenture yield rises to 3.1 pct - traders.
newsitem.headline: NCB debenture yield rises to 3.1 pct - traders.

text.p: A five-year bank debenture with a 2.15 percent coupon issued by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) in December was traded at a yield of 3.10 percent in the secondary market on Tuesday, bond traders said.
Meanwhile, a five-year debenture with a 1.6 percent coupon issued by the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd was traded at a yield of 1.76 percent.
As a result, the spread between the yields of the IBJ and NCB debentures has widened to 134 basis points.
IBJ will announce its long-term prime rate and the coupon for January five-year debentures on Wednesday, an official at the bank said.
NCB is expected to announce its long-term prime rate and January debenture coupon on Thursday.
Asked what terms might be set for the new debenture after a rise in the secondary market yield, an official at NCB said: "We are still considering them at this stage."
The prime rate, at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, was cut by 0.2 percentage point to a historical low of 2.5 percent in December.
